title: Trapped in a Toxic Relationship With a Bad App? It’s Time to Break Free!
text: We’ve all been there. An app you once adored no longer brings you any joy. It’s grown buggy and frustrating over time, or a botched update turned it into something unusable. You’ve probably thought about dumping it. But after years of handing over your personal data, you gave up and stayed stuck in this stale, joyless relationship. Why? Because moving to a new, potentially better app felt harder than putting up with the bugs and bizarre design changes of the bad one. Just look at Evernote. After nearly a decade of luring in millions of users, the company last year slammed the brakes on free use of its software while jacking up prices for its plans by as much as 40 percent. And this month? Evernote rolled out a redesign of its mobile app that users blasted as bloated with useless features, making simple note taking far too complex. Yet people are still clinging to Evernote, partly because getting their notes out is anything but easy. “We understand those kind of changes don’t make everyone happy,” said Greg Chiemingo, an Evernote spokesman. “In fact, we’ve seen continued growth of paying customers over the last two years.” Seriously? People deserve far better than this! Every single day you waste on a bad app is time you could be spending with a superior product that will make your life better. Here are my tips, drawn from interviews and personal experience, for making a clean break. No app is perfect, but at some point you have to draw the line. The trouble is, you may be stuck in such a rut that you can’t even see the warning signs. The most obvious one: an app stops working reliably in a way that affects your life.

title: UN Sounds the Alarm: Stop Sending Migrants Back to Hungary’s Razor-Wire Camps!
text: Enough! European countries must stop sending asylum seekers back to Hungary, where conditions for new arrivals, including children, are getting worse and abuse is alleged, the United Nations said Monday. Conditions for asylum seekers and other migrants in Hungary have long been considered dire. But they have deteriorated even further since the country last month brought in a new law ordering the systematic detention of all asylum seekers. “I urge states to suspend any Dublin transfer of to this country until the Hungarian authorities bring their practices and policies in line with European and international law,” said Filippo Grandi, United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees. The Dublin Regulation, meant to stop people from making asylum claims in multiple countries by requiring asylum seekers to be sent back to the first European country they arrived in, applies to European Union nations as well as Switzerland and Norway. Grandi said he was “encouraged” by a European Commission decision to work with Hungarian authorities to bring Budapest’s practices in line with EU law. But he stressed in a statement that “urgent measures are needed to improve access to asylum in Hungary.” Urgent indeed! The UN refugee agency has warned again and again that Hungary’s physical barriers and restrictive policies effectively deny the access to asylum guaranteed under international law. And the reality is grim. Since Hungary’s new law came into force on March 28, all new asylum seekers, including children, have been “detained in shipping containers surrounded by high razor fences at the border for the entire length of their asylum procedures,” UNHCR pointed out. Children! According to the government, 324 shipping container homes have been installed at two separate locations called “transit zones,” built into a fence that Hungary put up along the border in 2015.

title: AI system predicts Trump election win and greater popularity than Obama
text: An artificial intelligence (AI) system that correctly predicted the outcome of the last three presidential elections has predicted that Donald Trump will win the 2016 election. The MogIA system has calculated that Donald Trump will not only win the election but will also prove a more popular choice than Barack Obama was in 2008. CNBC reported that MogIA was developed by Sanjiv Rai, the founder of Indian start-up Genic.ai. The system takes in 20 million data points from public platforms in the U.S., including Google, Facebook, Twitter and YouTube, and analyzes the information to produce predictions. The AI system was created in 2004 and has continued to improve since then. It had already correctly predicted the results of the Democratic and Republican primaries. The system takes into account data such as engagement with tweets and Facebook Live videos. According to the results, Trump has exceeded the engagement numbers of Barack Obama’s peak in 2008, the year Obama came to power, by 25 percent.

title: Growing number of Americans leaving the United States permanently
text: Many Americans are currently considering whether conditions in the United States have become bad enough to leave the country for good, and an increasing number are choosing to leave the country of their birth permanently. Some are leaving for tax reasons, some because they believe the future is brighter elsewhere, and others because they are very concerned about the direction in which the country is heading and do not expect a turnaround any time soon. Several of the author’s friends and contacts who regard themselves as “preppers” have decided that the United States is too far gone to recover. They have moved their families out of the country and do not plan to return. As the country continues along its current troubled path, this trend is likely to accelerate further. Some Americans are also renouncing their citizenship when they leave. They represent only a small percentage of those leaving the country, but as Bloomberg recently reported, the number of Americans who renounced their citizenship in the second quarter of 2013 was six times larger than the number who renounced their citizenship in the second quarter of the previous year: “Americans renouncing U.S. citizenship surged sixfold in the second quarter from a year earlier as the government prepares to introduce tougher asset-disclosure rules. Expatriates giving up their nationality at U.S. embassies climbed to 1,131 in the three months through June from 189 in the year-earlier period, according to Federal Register figures published today.”

title: Harassment Scandal Rocks Westminster: Theresa May ‘Very Concerned’ as Parliament’s Dark Secret Emerges
text: Now the scandal has reached the heart of British power! It named no one in connection with the allegations, but cited unnamed members of the group when describing its contents and purpose. Who are these predators? “The reports are very concerning, but I can’t pre-empt allegations or investigations that haven’t come to light yet,” May’s spokeswoman said when asked about the Sun story. “The prime minister was very clear when we responded to the reports about Harvey Weinstein in the last few weeks that any unwanted sexual behavior is completely unacceptable, and that is true in any walk of life including politics.” And the trouble doesn’t end there. title: Sheriff Joe Arpaio to face criminal prosecution
text: After 20 years of corruption, millions of dollars spent on ethics charges and damage to the integrity of law enforcement, Sheriff Joe Arpaio will face criminal prosecution. After Arpaio was found guilty of contempt of court in civil court, U.S. District Court Judge Murray Snow, a Republican appointee, recommended that prosecutors bring criminal charges against Arpaio, his second-in-command Gerard Sheridan, and Maricopa County Sheriff’s Office Captain Steve Bailey. Arpaio’s attorney, Michele Iafrate, was also recommended for prosecution. Two months ago, Arpaio, Sheridan, Bailey and Iafrate were found guilty in civil court of violating court orders to halt a practice of the Maricopa County Sheriff’s Office that included elements of racial profiling. The Office, at Arpaio’s direction, intentionally disregarded the orders, and those named in the civil suit lied about doing so, including under oath. In his order, Snow, who wrote 22 times that the defendants had intentionally broken the law and the court order, said: “Criminal contempt serves to vindicate the Court’s authority by punishing the intentional disregard for that authority.” Arpaio and his associates are therefore not above the law. While Republicans chanted “lock her up” at the RNC, one of the convention’s keynote speakers, Arpaio, is being brought before a court to face criminal charges. Arpaio’s legal team said it would appeal the decision in civil court and challenge the recommendation for criminal charges. Even with Trump on the ticket, Arpaio is in a difficult contest to retain his position as Sheriff of Maricopa County.

title: ‘Do Not Try Us!’ Trump Unleashes Furious Warning to ‘Rogue Regime’ North Korea
text: The gloves are off! We will not be intimidated,” he told South Korean lawmakers. “And we will not let the worst atrocities in history be repeated here, on this ground we fought and died to secure.”

title: No Dictators, No Kings: Why the Libertarians Put the Flip-Floppers to Shame
text: What a breath of fresh air! Last week I moderated a "town hall" with the Libertarian presidential and vice presidential candidates, and it was refreshing, because Govs. Gary Johnson and William Weld actually respect limits on presidential power. On Sunday, when Fox's Chris Wallace went after Johnson's plan to replace the IRS with a consumption tax, Johnson pointed out that he's "not getting elected dictator or king." Wallace suggested that means, "Don't take my policies seriously because they won't get through." Wrong! It means Johnson understands that America is a constitutional republic, and there are (and ought to be) checks on what presidents can do. Responding to Wallace's jab about Johnson not taking his own promises seriously, Johnson shot back, "Take them very seriously. Count on certainty that we're always going to support taxes going lower... being in business being easier, rules and regulations not getting worse." Compare that with the rest of the field. Clinton flips positions from year to year: praising trade deals, then condemning them; condemning gay marriage, then praising it – then scolding anyone who doesn't share her new position! Trump flips even faster, sometimes day to day. After vowing to deport millions of immigrants, now he says he won't if they pay taxes and fill out paperwork – roughly the same position Jeb Bush and Marco Rubio held when Trump trashed them! title: Advertisers Flee YouTube as Ads Land Next to Hate Speech – Is Online Advertising Broken?
text: When Google snapped up YouTube in 2006 for $1.65 billion, it looked like a pricey gamble – a bet that an online service notorious for pirated videos and vapid content could win over major advertisers. The bet paid off big. YouTube is now one of the pillars of Google’s advertising empire and the most valuable video platform on the internet. In recent years, advertisers who could not ignore its massive audience flocked to YouTube to reach younger people who have started to shun traditional broadcast television. But now the technology powering YouTube’s ad business is under fierce scrutiny, as AT&T, Johnson & Johnson and other marketers announce they are pulling their ads from the service. Why? The automated system that buys and places ads online has too often landed brands right next to offensive material on YouTube, such as hate speech. On Thursday, the service Lyft became the latest to bail, yanking its ads after they appeared next to videos from a racist skinhead group. “This is beyond offensive,” a Lyft spokesman, Scott Coriell, said. “As soon as we learned of it, we pulled our advertising on YouTube.” This exodus strikes at the very core of YouTube’s appeal. Unlike television, with specific programming in which brands choose to run their advertising, YouTube mirrors the internet’s sprawl, specializing in niche content that may not appeal to a mainstream audience but attracts engaged viewers. The result? An enormous audience watching one billion hours of videos a day – perfect for new ad technology that minutely slices and dices an audience so companies can target specific viewers.

title: Fired! Trump Dumps Campaign Manager Corey Lewandowski in Dramatic Shake-Up
text: He’s out! Donald Trump fired his hard-charging campaign manager, Corey Lewandowski, on Monday in a dramatic shake-up meant to calm panicked Republican leaders and turn around one of the most chaotic stretches of Trump’s unconventional White House bid. Lewandowski, in some ways as brash and unconventional as the candidate himself, had been at Trump’s side from the very start of his unlikely rise to presumptive GOP nominee. But he clashed with veteran operatives brought in to make the seat-of-the-pants campaign more professional. The former conservative activist played a central role in daily operations, fundraising and Trump’s search for a running mate – but his aggressive approach also fueled near-constant infighting that complicated Trump’s pivot to the general election. Reached on Monday, Lewandowski brushed off criticism of his approach and pointed the finger at campaign chairman Paul Manafort. "Paul Manafort has been in operational control of the campaign since April 7. That's a fact," Lewandowski said, refusing to elaborate on his dismissal. Asked by CNN why he was fired, he said: "I don't know the answer to that." Really? Lewandowski also insists his relationships with Trump’s top adviser, Paul Manafort, and the candidate’s daughter, Ivanka, are good. He was fired Monday after a turbulent period for the campaign, marked by infighting and rumors. Spokeswoman Hope Hicks said in a statement earlier in the day that she wishes Lewandowski the best. He is the chairman of the New Hampshire Republican Party's delegation to the GOP national convention. Trump spokeswoman Hope Hicks called Lewandowski's exit a "parting of ways." But a person close to Trump said Lewandowski was forced out largely because of his poor relationship with the Republican National Committee and GOP officials. That person spoke on condition of anonymity because the person was not authorized to discuss internal deliberations.
